description: Answers the owner's 'is g₂ fitted to AME / larger context?' question. g₂ is NOT a tuned parameter, but r = g₂−1 is a FRAME ARTIFACT: across equally-valid O(t²) conventions for removing the same bar-odd tier, r swings over [−3.4%, +7.4%] — a spread ≈12× the signal |r|≈0.87%, so r is ~90% convention, not physics. Structurally, Ω_{k≥2}=0 exactly for the deuteron σ₁³ (single generator), so the bar-even h² correction is a character/frame projection, NOT a dynamical Magnus term — g₂=1 is near-definitional and r is the frame residual. The REAL robust result is the tier convergence: B(deuteron) predicted to 0.036% (360 ppm) from q₀ via three derived tiers (rotational, bar-odd t, bar-even h² unit). Larger context: the well-defined open problem is B(deuteron) below ~0.04% (the Δ_λ closure), NOT the frame-dependent r. scope-(a), audit-only, nothing wired; no fit, no AME inversion.
tier: frame-sensitivity measurement + tier convergence + Ω_{k≥2}=0 structural locate; answers the owner question; no fit

F3_bar_even_is_projection_not_dynamics.omega_k_ge_2: 0 exactly (deuteron word σ₁³ is a single generator; every [a,a]=0)
F3_bar_even_is_projection_not_dynamics.meaning: the bar-even h² correction is NOT a Magnus/holonomy dynamical term (all vanish) — it is the character/frame projection of the order-h² unit. So g₂=1 is near-definitional (natural order-h² frame unit, coeff 1); r is the frame residual, not a categorical amplitude.
